statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete. The requested US URL geolocated to the Yahoo UK surface; findings apply to the observed UK portal, consent, Finance, Search, News article, and login templates.

page.framework: Next.js on the current Yahoo homepage; mixed Yahoo properties use distinct stacks
page.notes: Representative 6-path audit. The consent handoff was assessed as part of the public entry experience. Not covered: authenticated account settings, mail inbox, finance transaction/watchlist mutation, checkout/subscription, video playback, and every regional/template variant.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark preference matched but entry surfaces stayed light.
Seven 700ms animations remained running under reduce.
Lighthouse contrast passed and controls/text remained visually distinct.

checkOutcomes.method: Transition video plus static markup probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Consent-to-home navigation is abrupt and no view-transition declarations were found.

checkOutcomes.method: Static CSS probe and mobile layout observation
checkOutcomes.evidence: No scroll-linked visual effect or scroll animation was present, so no main-thread imitation was observed.
Sampled pages use native scrolling and ordinary controls without custom pointer gesture traps.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile screenshots and static feature probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Long feed chrome has no observed scroll-state response or progress cue.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/static feature probe of menus and consent overlay
checkOutcomes.evidence: Positioned UI was present but no anchor-positioning usage/fallback declarations were found.
Strong headline hierarchy, skip links, market strip, and visible state labels direct attention.
Blocking consent overlay obscures all content on entry.
Visible modal has zero dialog/popover elements.
Once content is visible, Finance uses a content-dense hierarchy with restrained chrome.

checkOutcomes.method: Layout at 360x800 on homepage and Finance
checkOutcomes.evidence: Both measured zero horizontal overflow with viewport metadata.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw/static CSS feature probe across portal templates
checkOutcomes.evidence: No container-query declarations were found for reused portal components.
Target-size audit passed; sampled native links/buttons expose browser focus outlines and mobile controls are adequately sized.
Homepage/search/Finance communicate purpose with prominent search, headlines, and clear primary controls.
Representative web search returned HTTP 500 instead of results.
Search failure states the problem and preserves a retry query; nonexistent path returns a real 404.
Lighthouse LCP was 4.1s/FCP 3.6s and Finance had two long tasks.
Homepage and Finance observers measured CLS 0 with no recorded shifts.

checkOutcomes.method: Finance layout and HAR script totals
checkOutcomes.evidence: Finance recorded 64ms/107ms long tasks and homepage loaded 90 scripts.
4.12MB/278 requests with blocking CSS and cache gaps.
2.14MB scripts, third-party dominance, and 53KiB estimated unused CSS.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits and DOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Visible-label/accessibility-name mismatch and landmark omission were detected.
Automated contrast audit passed and text/controls were legible in sampled states.
Consent page has no landmarks and lacks lang; sampled controls include inconsistent focus styling.
Body and headline text are readable with comfortable sizing and wrapping on sampled views.
Viewport restricts scaling and mobile consent requires a forced scroll-to-end step.
No browser console errors were logged on the audited entry.
Doctype/charset are valid, but six entry images lack dimensions and CSS waste is reported.
Two BFCache blockers were reported.
Consent handoff exposes a generic title and no meta description despite good underlying Yahoo metadata.
Server HTML has 47 real anchors, viewport metadata, and general crawler access; layout has no overflow.
Public homepage returned 200 in recon, has a canonical, robots permits general crawling, and declares a sitemap.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw static metadata probe and article capture
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage contains two JSON-LD blocks and the article template presents a coherent visible entity.
HTTPS and no exposed secrets passed, but key security headers are missing on the final entry response.
194 third-party requests transferred 2.77MB after consent.
No permission prompt appeared on load; login source contains WebAuthn capability.
CSP/frame protection/HSTS/Permissions-Policy were absent on the consent response.
Homepage ships 533KB server HTML with content/links; discoverability reports 100% raw coverage and no JS shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Responsive screenshots and consent interaction video
checkOutcomes.evidence: Consent choices remain reachable and reject navigation completes; sampled overlays did not clip horizontally.

checkOutcomes.method: Site-type judgement and Finance manifest probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: A public news/search portal is not a core offline application; Finance exposes a manifest, but offline installability is not required for the audited core content.
checkOutcomes.reason: A public news/search portal is not a core offline application; Finance exposes a manifest, but offline installability is not required for the audited core content.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Search failure gives a retry action and the bad content route returns a branded 404 response.
Underlying Yahoo/Finance use en-GB, but the consent document has an empty lang attribute.
UK market values, percentages, and relative article times are formatted coherently for the en-GB surface.
The sampled landing, article, search, and sign-in surfaces expose no user-scheduled or cross-time-zone event workflow to validate.
checkOutcomes.reason: The sampled landing, article, search, and sign-in surfaces expose no user-scheduled or cross-time-zone event workflow to validate.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Accept all and Reject all have equal visual prominence; manage settings and withdrawal policy are explicit.
Failure message is neutral, preserves the query, and gives a clear retry action.
Username field omits autocomplete=username.
Sampled sign-in entry is concise, labels persistence, offers federated sign-in, and links account creation/terms.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR weight offenders and image probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: A 444KB image and multiple large media assets load in the initial portal graph.
Initial window loads 278 requests including analytics/ad background calls and 90 scripts.
2.77MB third-party bytes and 4.12MB total are disproportionate for first view.
Yahoo explicitly disallows major AI/search-agent crawlers and exposes no declared agent tool surface; this indicates no intended agent-facing capability.
checkOutcomes.reason: Yahoo explicitly disallows major AI/search-agent crawlers and exposes no declared agent tool surface; this indicates no intended agent-facing capability.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No user-facing inference task requiring built-in on-device AI was present in the sampled news/search/account journeys.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user-facing inference task requiring built-in on-device AI was present in the sampled news/search/account journeys.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline/post heap totals after ten scroll cycles
checkOutcomes.evidence: Repeated scrolling changed heap nodes only 72,846→72,861 and self size 3,823,114→3,824,698 bytes, showing no unbounded growth in the sampled interaction.
Consent entry footprint was 72,846 nodes and 3.82MB self size, proportionate to the sampled document.

Total node population remained effectively flat across ten cycles (+15), with no accumulation signal; constructor-level detached-node tracing was not needed to establish growth absence at this confidence.

principleOutcomes.reason: Yahoo explicitly disallows major AI/search-agent crawlers and exposes no declared agent tool surface; this indicates no intended agent-facing capability. No user-facing inference task requiring built-in on-device AI was present in the sampled news/search/account journeys.

paths.description: Yahoo UK homepage and consent entry surface, representing the public portal landing page and consent journey.
Representative Yahoo News article/detail template discovered from homepage links.
Yahoo Finance listing/content portal, representing a distinct data-rich app-like template.
Primary Yahoo web-search result journey for the query “web platform”.
Representative account sign-in entry flow, checked for input assistance and modern authentication signals.
Representative nonexistent Yahoo content route, checked for HTTP/error-state recovery.

findings.summary: The main Yahoo and consent surfaces do not adapt to the requested dark theme.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated homepage screenshot is pixel-identical in its white consent surface to the normal desktop capture; the computed preference probe confirms prefers-color-scheme: dark while body text remains black on a transparent/light surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use preference-driven surface/text tokens, using light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme fallback so the consent and portal UI retint together.

findings.summary: Yahoo Finance continues non-essential animation when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion runtime probe found seven running animations, each 700ms, while matchMedia(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) was true.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove or shorten non-essential transitions and stop auto-advancing motion while preserving state feedback.

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes do not expose modern declarative transition or positioning cues.
findings.evidence: The consent-to-home video shows an abrupt full-document swap, and raw/static probes found no view-transition or scroll-timeline declarations and no container-query use on the homepage surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route/state changes with View Transitions and use declarative scroll/anchor/container primitives where those components need positional adaptation, retaining fallbacks.

findings.summary: A mandatory consent interstitial obscures the entire homepage and every article before content can be used.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, and article screenshots all show a modal privacy wall over blurred or dimmed content. On mobile the long copy extends beyond the viewport and requires a “Go to end” control before the choices are visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving consent surface with equivalent accept/reject controls immediately visible; reserve blocking modality only where legally necessary and make it fit without a forced scroll.

findings.summary: The blocking consent experience is not represented by the native dialog or popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe reports dialogs: 0 and popovers: 0 while screenshots show a modal overlay; no landmark exists on the consent document.
findings.suggestedFix: Represent the modal flow with <dialog>, manage initial/return focus, provide an explicit close or equivalent choice, and use popover only for non-modal transient UI.

findings.summary: The primary web-search journey failed instead of returning results.
findings.evidence: A direct Yahoo search for “web platform” returned HTTP 500 and the captured result page says “We had temporary problems searching for web pages,” offering only a retry link.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore reliable search-result delivery and preserve the query with a clear retry path and fallback result source during upstream failures.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a very heavy, third-party-dominated request graph after consent.
findings.evidence: The post-consent HAR recorded 278 requests and 4,120,910 transferred bytes: 90 scripts (2,137,452 bytes), 194 third-party requests (2,772,039 bytes), multiple render-blocking stylesheets, and missing cache headers. Lighthouse on the consent entry measured LCP 4.1s and FCP 3.6s; Finance recorded 64ms and 107ms long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a first-load budget; remove or defer low-value ad/analytics bundles, split non-critical code, prioritize the LCP resource, shorten blocking CSS chains, and fix cache policy for stable assets.

findings.summary: The consent entry restricts zoom and has accessibility semantics gaps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports user-scalable=no or maximum-scale below 5, a visible-label/accessibility-name mismatch, and a missing html lang attribute. The consent DOM has no landmarks; the 360px screenshot requires an extra “Go to end” step to reach choices.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow pinch zoom, add the correct lang and landmarks, align accessible names with visible labels, and ensure all choices remain reachable and understandable at narrow/zoomed layouts.

findings.summary: The entry surface has asset sizing and browser lifecycle hygiene problems.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found six images without width/height on the consent entry, and Lighthouse reports two reasons preventing back/forward cache restoration plus 53 KiB estimated unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Give images intrinsic dimensions/aspect-ratio, remove BFCache blockers, and trim or conditionally load unused consent CSS.

findings.summary: The browser-visible consent landing replaces Yahoo’s descriptive metadata with generic, incomplete metadata.
findings.evidence: The browser and non-JS discoverability capture resolve to “Your privacy choices”; Lighthouse reports no meta description. The underlying raw Yahoo HTML does contain a descriptive title, description, canonical, and server-rendered links, so the loss is specific to the consent entry.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve page-specific title, description, canonical, and social metadata through the consent handoff while keeping the consent purpose clear to users.

findings.summary: The browser-visible entry response lacks important browser-enforced security policies.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found HTTPS but no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy on the final consent response. A separate rate-limited Yahoo response exposed nosniff and a weak no-referrer-when-downgrade policy but still no CSP/HSTS evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP including frame-ancestors, HSTS, nosniff, strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or stricter), and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy consistently across Yahoo and consent origins.

findings.summary: Third-party advertising and analytics dominate the post-consent network footprint.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributes 194 of 278 requests and 2.77 MB of 4.12 MB to third-party origins, including Google Ads/Tag Manager, Taboola, Scorecard Research, and Yahoo analytics calls; some analytics/beacon responses lacked cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit each vendor against user value, remove redundant measurement, defer non-essential tags until the relevant consent state, batch analytics, and isolate remaining third parties.

findings.summary: The consent document omits its language declaration.
findings.evidence: The runtime DOM probe reports an empty html lang on “Your privacy choices,” while the underlying Yahoo and Finance documents correctly use en-GB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set html lang=en-GB (and dir when needed) on the consent document and verify shared components use logical properties for bidirectional layouts.

findings.summary: The Yahoo sign-in username field does not advertise the expected autocomplete token.
findings.evidence: The login probe found a text input named username with an empty autocomplete attribute. WebAuthn-related source was present, but no visible passkey choice appeared on the sampled first step.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete=username on the identifier field and expose passkey sign-in or conditional mediation clearly when available, retaining password/federated fallbacks.

findings.summary: Media, scripts, and background third-party work are disproportionate for the first portal view.
findings.evidence: The post-consent load transferred 4.12 MB, including a 444 KB decorative/highlight image, 2.14 MB of scripts, and 2.77 MB from third parties; analytics and advertising calls continue during the initial observation window.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a page-weight and third-party budget, responsive/modern image delivery, lazy activation for recommendations and ads, and background-fetch prioritization tied to visibility and consent.

taskList.title: Cut initial request, script, third-party, and media weight behind a strict budget
Replace the content-blocking consent wall with a compact, semantic, zoom-safe flow
Deploy consistent CSP, HSTS, clickjacking, referrer, and permissions policies
Restore reliable search result completion with resilient retry behavior
Honor dark and reduced-motion preferences across shared Yahoo surfaces
Preserve descriptive metadata across the consent handoff
Fix image dimensions, BFCache blockers, and username autofill
Progressively enhance navigation and reusable components with declarative transitions and queries
